subject: Discovery: inference cost and optimization — recap & next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@datascale.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Oct 2025 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery: inference cost and optimization — recap & next steps

Alex — thanks again for the 30-min intro today. Quick recap from my side so we’re aligned and can move toward a concrete next step. I’ve attached the cost snapshot you shared during the call for reference.

Key pain points you highlighted:
- Token cost and surprise CPU/GPU spend on peak inference runs (monthly variance ~2.5x).
- Latency-sensitive features (snippet generation) that degrade when batch sizes increase.
- Lack of effective reuse (no prefix/KV caching today) causing repeated token compute.
- Concern about model quantization impacting downstream accuracy/regulatory traceability.

Current stack (what you said):
- Frontend: Go microservices + NGINX edge
- Inference: Managed GPU endpoints (shared pooled VMs); service does per-request cold start ~50–200ms extra
- Models: mix of open LLMs (Llama 2 variants) and a proprietary fine-tune for prompts
- Observability: basic Prom/Grafana, no per-token cost breakdown

Success criteria (how you’ll evaluate a solution):
1) Reduce per-100k-token cost by >= 30% without >10% degradation in accuracy for the top-3 prompt sets.
2) Maintain 95th percentile latency < 450ms for snippet generation at expected production QPS.
3) Clear auditability on quantization/weights changes for compliance.

What we see as feasible given your constraints (tentative):
- Batch-aware routing + adaptive batching to reduce token cost during steady-state without impacting tail latency.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeat prompts (we estimated ~18–32% token reuse from your example flows).
- Offer quantization path: PTQ int8 as first step (minimal accuracy impact), then evaluate 4-bit only for non-regulated prompt tiers.

Immediate next steps (agreed):
- You to share the sample traffic CSV / kgps traces and the cost snapshot (attached). (Alex)
- Redwood (Rachel + Vivek) to produce a 2-slide sketch: expected unit-economics with batching/caching + risk notes on quantization (ETA: 3 business days). (Rachel)
- Schedule a 60-min technical workshop with your infra and ours to walk model/serving constraints (propose next Wed or Thu).

Attachments: [Attachment: datascale-cost-snapshot.xlsx (Excel, 96KB)]

If I missed anything or mischaracterized priorities, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll ping Rachel and Vivek to start the cost/tech sketch.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0126

From: Alex Moreno <alex@datascale.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@datacloud.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 Oct 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery: inference cost and optimization — recap & next steps

Jonas — this is a good summary; thanks. A few clarifications so Rachel/Vivek can size correctly: 

1) Quantization constraints: we cannot deploy a 4-bit model for any throughput that touches PII-driven prompts due to our compliance team. We are OK with int8/PTQ on non-PII flows and can label prompts by tier.
2) QPS & latency: aiming for ~180 qps sustained across snippet endpoints, with 95th < 450ms as you noted. Peak observed bursts up to ~550 qps for ~90s.
3) Cacheability: roughly 25% repeat prefixes across our most-used prompt sets; additional reuse if we split prompts by user segment.

Two asks from us: 
- Can you include a quick-ballpark per-month cost delta in the sketch comparing current spend vs Redwood suggestions (assume steady-state 180 qps, 30M tokens/month)?
- Please call out which parts of the stack require code changes vs config (we’d prefer minimal changes to our Go path).

I’m copying Priya (Platform Eng) to coordinate the tech workshop scheduling. Happy for the Wed/Thu window; Thu afternoon Pacific would be best for our team.

Subject: Fwd: Discovery: inference cost and optimization — recap & next steps (internal)

Quick internal: Alex confirmed constraints and asked for a ballpark cost delta at 30M tokens/month and a clear split code vs config.

Rachel — can you and your SE team draft the 2-slide sketch (unit economics w/ table + latency risk notes) by EOD Wed? Include assumptions and best/worse case. Reference the attached datascale-cost-snapshot.xlsx.

Vivek — can you validate whether caching (prefix/KV) is deployable with their current managed GPU endpoints or if we need a routing shim in front? If a shim is required, give rough dev & infra hours.

I’ll propose Thu 21 Oct 10:30am PT for the tech workshop to Alex/Priya.

Thanks —
Jonas

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Discovery: inference cost and optimization — recap & next steps

Alex/Priya — thanks for the confirmations and for sharing constraints. Confirming the next steps and attachments: 

1) Technical workshop: Thu, 21 Oct 2025, 10:30am PT — invite sent (60min). Aim: review model access, routing, caching feasibility, and quantization gating.
2) Deliverables from Redwood before workshop (attached):
   - 2-slide unit-economics sketch (redwood-pricing-model.csv) covering batching + caching scenarios and estimated monthly delta at 30M tokens.
   - Draft SLA / deployment notes (sla-draft.pdf) highlighting rollback and audit options for quantization changes.
3) Action for DataScale: send a 1-hour sample trace or production traffic CSV if possible (helps us model batching gains).

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood-pricing-model.csv (CSV, 12KB)] [Attachment: sla-draft.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

If Thu 10:30am PT doesn’t work, propose two alternatives and we’ll adjust. Looking forward — we’ll aim to show a conservative (safe) and optimistic (max-efficiency) path so legal/compliance has options.

Cheers,
